title: Developing Shiny Web Applications
text: Suppose following shiny web application: migrate app within CSIAPPS ecosystem, can leverage several functions provided csiapps.
code: library(shiny)  df = faithful[, 2]  ui <- fluidPage(      titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),      sidebarLayout(         sidebarPanel(             sliderInput("bins",                         "Number of bins:",                         min = 1,                         max = 50,                         value = 30)         ),          mainPanel(            plotOutput("distPlot")         )     ) )  server <- function(input, output) {      output$distPlot <- renderPlot({         bins <- seq(min(df), max(df), length.out = input$bins + 1)          hist(df, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white',              xlab = 'Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)',              main = 'Histogram of waiting times')     }) }  shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Sandbox Mode
text: Putting together — registration warehouse workflows one script, local, network: code deployed, disable sandbox mode let CSIAPPS team set SOURCE_UUID real warehouse uuid provision — app code unchanged. developer never handles real uuid, schema registration step 5 development-scaffolding: production schema already lives remote warehouse.
code: library(csiapps)  # 1. (Optional) simulate login for a wrapped app's /me header Sys.setenv(CSIAPPS_ACCESS_TOKEN = "your-dev-access-token") set_institute("csiontario") check_secrets()  # 2. Point the app at a placeholder source (CSIAPPS sets the real one in production) Sys.setenv(SOURCE_UUID = "dev-placeholder")  # 3. Seed the registration registry org <- create_sport_org("Rowing Canada") create_profile(3, org$id, first_names = c("Ada", "Blair", "Cai"),                           last_names  = c("Nkemelu", "Okafor", "Zhang"))  # 4. Read it back like production orgs     <- fetch_org_options() athletes <- fetch_profiles(filters = list(sport_org_id = org$id))  # 5. Register a warehouse schema and ingest records keyed to those athletes register_sandbox_schema(Sys.getenv("SOURCE_UUID"), '{   "type": "object",   "required": ["athlete_id", "weight"],   "properties": {     "athlete_id": {"type": "integer"},     "weight":     {"type": "number"}   } }')  make_request(   endpoint = "api/warehouse/ingestion/primary/",   method   = "POST",   body = list(     source        = Sys.getenv("SOURCE_UUID"),     records       = list(       list(athlete_id = athletes[[1]]$id, weight = 72.5),       list(athlete_id = athletes[[2]]$id, weight = 68.1)     ),     subject_field = "athlete_id"   ) )  # 6. Pull the records back; subjects resolve to the registered athletes make_request(   endpoint = "api/warehouse/data-records",   query    = list(source_uuid = Sys.getenv("SOURCE_UUID")),   paginate = TRUE )  # 7. Reset when done clear_sandbox()

what: Worked example: integrating third-party vendor data
title: Sandbox Mode
text: common real task joining third-party vendor’s data — testing platform, wearable, lab system — onto CSIAPPS athletes. CSI Ontario maintains AMS_mapping data source whose records link CSIAPPS athlete (id) athlete’s profile vendor system (vendor_profile_id, vendor_profile_name). consumer app reads AMS_mapping translate vendor’s ids canonical CSIAPPS athlete ids. production mapping already lives warehouse. build test consumer locally, reproduce miniature AMS_mapping source sandbox: create dummy athletes, author small mapping CSV whose id column matches dummy athletes whose vendor_profile_id column matches real vendor ids, ingest AMS_mapping schema, read back join — exactly production . Steps 1–4 (dummy athletes, schema registration, CSV ingestion) development-scaffolding. production AMS_mapping source already populated maintained upstream; read--join step 5 real app code, ships unchanged.

what: 5. Read the mapping back and join your vendor data
title: Sandbox Mode
text: part ships production. Pull AMS_mapping records, keep active ones, merge() real vendor data onto vendor_profile_id — every vendor measurement now carries canonical CSIAPPS id, can enrich fetch_profile(): active flag append-history. AMS_mapping append-: mapping corrected removed appending new record — tombstone active = FALSE, plus corrected record — recent record per (id, vendor, vendor_profile_id, vendor_profile_name) wins. production warehouse returns currently-active mappings (filtered server-side). sandbox returns every record ingest, unfiltered — ingest corrections testing, reduce latest record per identity keep active ones mirror production returns:
code: resp <- make_request(   endpoint = "api/warehouse/data-records",   query    = list(source_uuid = Sys.getenv("AMS_MAPPING_UUID")),   paginate = TRUE )  mapping <- do.call(rbind, lapply(resp[[1]]$results, function(r) data.frame(   id                = r$data$id,   vendor_profile_id = r$data$vendor_profile_id,   active            = r$data$active,   stringsAsFactors  = FALSE ))) mapping <- mapping[mapping$active, ] # consumers keep only active mappings  # your REAL third-party data, keyed by the vendor's own id vendor_data <- data.frame(   vendor_profile_id = c("VX-8841", "VX-8842", "VX-9001"),   resting_hr        = c(52, 58, 49),   stringsAsFactors  = FALSE )  joined <- merge(vendor_data, mapping, by = "vendor_profile_id") joined$athlete <- vapply(joined$id, function(i) {   p <- fetch_profile(profile_id = i)   paste(p$person$first_name, p$person$last_name) }, character(1)) joined # vendor_profile_id | resting_hr | id | active | athlete identity <- with(mapping, paste(id, vendor_profile_id)) # add vendor + name for the full key mapping  <- mapping[!duplicated(identity, fromLast = TRUE) & mapping$active, ]

what: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: Sandbox mode lets developers run full schema -> validate -> ingest -> retrieve warehouse workflow entirely locally, network access authentication. Sandbox mode enabled default, development work never reaches production warehouse accident: make_request() calls routed local, -memory warehouse instead REST API. disabled deployment options(csiapps.sandbox = FALSE) (setting CSIAPPS_ENV=production), can overridden per call sandbox argument make_request(). production sandbox workflows use calls, code changes needed moving development deployment. sandbox emulates three endpoints: GET api/warehouse/data-sources/{uuid} – returns schema previously registered register_sandbox_schema(), nested head_primary_definition$schema exactly like real API. POST api/warehouse/ingestion/primary/ – validates body$records registered schema body$source (using jsonvalidate) , success, stores memory writes JSON payload per-source folder disk inspection (see browse_sandbox()). GET api/warehouse/data-records – returns previously ingested records query$source_uuid, wrapped envelope (data, subject, created_at, ...) real API returns. endpoint raises error. Sandbox state lasts R session; use clear_sandbox() reset tests.

title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: Sandbox mode also lets wrapped Shiny app (see ui_wrapper(), server_wrapper(), check_secrets()) run locally without OAuth2 redirect. redirect exists obtain access token, requires client credentials safely distributed, sandbox mode server_wrapper() simulates login instead: seeds session developer's existing CSIAPPS_ACCESS_TOKEN hands code path production login . token used emulate login: present, /loaded real API header shows developer's real identity. data – sport organizations, athletes/profiles, warehouse records – served local sandbox (dummy registry emulated warehouse), never live API. token set, app shell still renders shows unauthenticated notice prompting developer set read-CSIAPPS_ACCESS_TOKEN. wrapped-app code runs modes; csiapps.sandbox option differs.

title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: access token used emulate login. wrapped app's /identity fetched real API token, set institute set_institute() match institute issued /rejected. Everything else dummy: sport organizations athletes come local registry (create_sport_org(), create_profile()) warehouse reads/writes emulated memory. real client data read. warehouse endpoints routed make_request(). Calling make_request("api/registration/...") sandbox raises 501; use fetch_org_options() / fetch_profiles() helpers, read dummy registry instead. sandbox, fetch_profiles() honours sport_org_id filter; filters ignored. sandbox faithfully simulates schema contract, warehouse. Anything depends server-side state differ production: Validation parity approximate. Sandbox ingestion validates records JSON Schema Ajv (via jsonvalidate), catches common failure modes (missing required fields, wrong types, length pattern violations). real server additionally enforces things schema express: resolution subject_field values registered profiles, duplicate/dataset handling existing data, token permissions. Validator implementations may also differ edge cases (e.g. format keyword enforcement). Passing sandbox validation therefore necessary sufficient condition production acceptance – treat green sandbox run guarantee. subject linkage emulated registered athletes. retrieval sandbox resolves record's subject_field value athletes registered create_profile() returns matched athlete (id, name, sport) record envelope, mirroring production. Resolution happens read time, athletes registered ingestion linked next read. athlete matches – none registered subject_field value mistyped – subject NULL rather fabricated. Production reject unresolved subject; sandbox accepts silently, green sandbox ingest guarantee server link every record.

Defaults is_sandbox_mode(), TRUE default. Disable sandbox mode globally options(csiapps.sandbox = FALSE) (CSIAPPS_ENV=production) route requests production warehouse.
